title: Finite-cover splittings and functorial deck action on pointed limits
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,x)$ with its profinite topology and left action on finite geometric fibres [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Finite etale covers are objects of [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. For every open normal subgroup $N\triangleleft\Pi$, let $(Y_N,y_N)$ be a pointed connected finite etale cover identified on its geometric fibre with $(\Pi/N,N)$, with pointed transition $Y_M\to Y_N$ inducing $aM\mapsto aN$ for $M\subseteq N$. Work in compatible universes and small indexing systems [def-weil-size-convention].
Let $(T,(p_N),t)$ be a limit of this system in schemes over $X$, with the compatible marked point, and assume $T$ is connected. For every finite etale $X$-scheme $Y$, write $E=Y_x$. There are unique $X$-maps $f_s:T\to Y$ for $s\in E$ with $f_s(t)=s$, and the map
$$\coprod_{s\in E}T\longrightarrow T\times_XY,\qquad z\text{ in summand }s\longmapsto(z,f_s(z))$$
is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. This includes $E=\varnothing$. For every $N$ acting trivially on $E$, $f_s$ factors as $f_{s,N}p_N$, where $f_{s,N}:Y_N\to Y$ is the unique finite-etale map with fibre formula $aN\mapsto as$. These maps are compatible with every refinement $M\subseteq N$; they are independent of such $N$, and for every finite-etale $X$-map $b:Y\to Z$ they satisfy $bf_s=f_{b(s)}$.
There are unique automorphisms $d_g:T\to T$ over $X$, for $g\in\Pi$, such that $p_Nd_g=f_{gN}$ for every $N$. They satisfy $f_sd_g=f_{gs}$, $d_1=1$, and $d_hd_g=d_{gh}$; thus $z\cdot g=d_g(z)$ is a right action normalized by the left monodromy on finite fibres.
For any pointed morphism $f:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ with the same hypotheses, a connected pointed limit $T'$ of the corresponding system, and $\Pi'=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X',x')$, there is a unique map $F:T'\to T$ over $f$ carrying $t'$ to $t$. If $\tau_Y:(f^*Y)_{x'}\simeq Y_x$ is the base-change fibre bijection, then $f_sF$ is the composite $T'\xrightarrow{f'_{\tau_Y^{-1}(s)}}f^*Y\to Y$. For the induced continuous homomorphism $f_*:\Pi'\to\Pi$, one has $Fd'_h=d_{f_*(h)}F$ for every $h\in\Pi'$. These pointed maps respect identities and composition.

proof.text: Finite-stage maps. By [def-galois-fibre-functor], E is a finite continuous left Pi-set. The kernel K of its permutation action is open and normal: it is the intersection of the stabilizers of the finitely many elements, each open by continuity, and is a kernel. This also gives K=Pi for E empty. For any open normal N contained in K and s in E, the formula aN ↦ as is well-defined and Pi-equivariant. By the equivalence of [thm-galois-fundamental] it gives a unique X-map f_{s,N}:Y_N→Y. Every equivariant map Pi/N→E is determined by N, since aN=a·N, so this is precisely the unique finite-etale map carrying y_N to s. Put f_s=f_{s,N}∘p_N for the moment; it carries t to s.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text: Graph splitting on the connected limit. The finite-stage formula supplies an X-map f_s for each geometric fibre point s. Regard the graph coproduct and T×_X Y as finite etale T-schemes. At the point t their geometric fibres are both E: every geometric point of the coproduct factors through one summand, whose map to T forces its first component to equal t, and the graph has second component s. Thus the graph map is bijective on this fibre. The finite-etale fibre functor reflects isomorphisms by [thm-galois-fundamental], so the graph cofan is colimiting. This argument applies unchanged for empty E and avoids a separate finite-stage coproduct and its pullback.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text: Pointwise uniqueness on any connected source. Pull Y back to the connected source T. Two X-maps T→Y agreeing at t give two maps from the identity cover of T to this finite-etale pullback, with equal evaluations at t. The identity cover is connected; evaluation on maps out of a connected object is injective in the Galois category supplied by [thm-galois-fundamental]. The two pullback lifts agree, hence their projections to Y agree. This proves marked-point uniqueness directly, without factoring arbitrary maps through a finite stage or first using the splitting. Composing with limit projections gives the analogous uniqueness for maps into any specified pointed coset limit.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text: Refinements, independence and cover naturality. For M contained in N, the fibre formulas for f_{s,N} followed after the pointed transition Y_M→Y_N and for f_{s,M} are both aM ↦ as, hence their maps agree by faithfulness in [thm-galois-fundamental]. After composition with p_M this gives the same map on T. For two subgroups killing E use their intersection to compare both maps, so the temporary definition of f_s in step 1 is independent of N and factors through every such N. Alternatively both maps agree at t and step 3 applies. For b:Y→Z finite etale over X, b∘f_s is an X-map taking t to b(s), hence equals f_{b(s)} by step 3. These arguments give exactly the stated transition and naturality formulas.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text:
Deck maps and their order. For g in Pi, the maps f_{gN}:T→Y_N are a compatible cone: under Y_M→Y_N their labels gM become gN by step 4 (the transition's fibre formula is part of the hypotheses). The universal property of the given limit supplies a unique X-map d_g with p_N∘d_g=f_{gN}. Fix Y,s and choose N killing its fibre E. Naturality in step 4 for f_{s,N}:Y_N→Y gives
f_s∘d_g=f_{s,N}∘p_N∘d_g=f_{s,N}∘f_{gN}=f_{gs}.
The last label follows from the equivariant finite-stage formula aN ↦ as established using [thm-galois-fundamental]. For g=1, f_N=p_N by step 3, so all projections give d_1=id. Moreover
p_N∘d_h∘d_g=f_{hN}∘d_g=f_{ghN}=p_N∘d_{gh}.
Equality of all limit legs gives d_h∘d_g=d_{gh}. Taking h=g^{-1} and then g=h^{-1} shows that d_{g^{-1}} is a two-sided inverse to d_g. The uniqueness of each d_g is already the uniqueness of the limit lift. Thus z·g=d_g(z) is the normalized right action with exactly the convention in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text:
Pointed maps of limits. Write f:X'→X and q_Y:f^*Y→Y for the projection. By [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] the base-change fibre bijections are tau_Y(z)=q_Y∘z, natural in Y, and there is a continuous homomorphism f_* with f_*(h)tau_Y(z)=tau_Y(hz); this is the base-change clause of [thm-galois-fundamental] with the bijection made explicit. For each N put r_N=tau_{Y_N}^{-1}(N), and define u_N=q_{Y_N}∘f'_{r_N}:T'→Y_N. The primed form of step 4 and naturality of tau show compatibility under every transition Y_M→Y_N. Also u_N(t')=q_{Y_N}∘r_N=tau_{Y_N}(r_N)=y_N, by the explicit formula for tau. The universal property of the X-limit supplies F:T'→T over f with p_N∘F=u_N; equality of all projected points gives F(t')=t. If G:T'→T is any other such pointed map, the pair (T'→X',p_N∘G) gives a map T'→f^*Y_N by [def-pc-fibre-product], taking t' to r_N. Primed step 3 makes it f'_{r_N}. Thus p_N∘G=u_N for every N and G=F. For arbitrary Y and s, the same fibre-product construction applied to f_s∘F takes t' to tau_Y^{-1}(s); primed step 3 gives
f_s∘F=q_Y∘f'_{tau_Y^{-1}(s)}.
This establishes existence, uniqueness and the full finite-cover comparison formula.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (1), (3); explicit finite-coset and limit-universal-property argument by Q86.

proof.text:
Equivariance and functoriality. Fix h in Pi', Y and s in E, and put r=tau_Y^{-1}(s). The equivariance of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] (the base-change clause of [thm-galois-fundamental]) reads tau_Y(hr)=f_*(h)s. Steps 5 and 6, first on X' and then on X, now give
f_s∘F∘d'_h=q_Y∘f'_r∘d'_h=q_Y∘f'_{hr}=f_{f_*(h)s}∘F=f_s∘d_{f_*(h)}∘F.
In particular take Y=Y_N and s=N, for which f_s=p_N. Equality on all limit legs proves F∘d'_h=d_{f_*(h)}∘F. The identity of T is a pointed lift over id_X, so uniqueness in step 6 makes it the identity comparison. For composable pointed morphisms the composite comparison is over the composite base morphism and sends the marked point to the marked point; the same uniqueness makes it the comparison for the composite. This proves all the stated functoriality clauses.
